questionText:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows:

"In January 1977, after nineteen months of authoritarian Emergency rule, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi unexpectedly announced that elections to the Lok Sabha would be held in March. Political prisoners were released, and censorship was relaxed. Seizing this democratic opening, the major opposition parties—Congress (O), Bharatiya Jana Sangh, Bharatiya Lok Dal, and the Socialist Party—united to form the Janata Party under the moral mentorship of Jayaprakash Narayan. Senior Congress leader Jagjivan Ram resigned from the cabinet and formed the Congress for Democracy, which aligned with Janata. The March 1977 general election was fought as a referendum on democracy versus dictatorship. The results were historic: the Janata alliance swept 330 seats, completely wiping out the Congress across the northern Hindi belt. Both Indira Gandhi and her son Sanjay suffered humiliating personal defeats in Rae Bareli and Amethi. On 24 March 1977, Morarji Desai was sworn in as the first non-Congress Prime Minister of independent India. In May 1977, the new government appointed the Shah Commission of Inquiry, headed by retired Chief Justice J.C. Shah, to investigate Emergency atrocities."

List-I (Name of Leaders) List-II (Their achievements)
(A) Maulana Abul
Kalam Azad
(I) Chairman, Drafting Committee of the
Constituent Assembly
(B) Rajkumari Amrit
Kaur
(II) Founder member of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh
(C) Bhimrao Ambedkar
(III) Education Minister in the first cabinet of free
India
(D) Deen Dayal
Upadhyaya
(IV) Minister of Health in the first cabinet of free
India
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Syllabus Core.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Syllabus Core (Crises of the Constitutional Order):
Matching leaders with their portfolios and contributions:
- (A) Maulana Abul Kalam Azad: First Minister of Education in free India -> (III)
- (B) Rajkumari Amrit Kaur: First Minister of Health in independent India -> (IV)
- (C) Bhimrao Ambedkar: Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and first Law Minister -> (I)
- (D) Deen Dayal Upadhyaya: Founding member and general secretary of Bharatiya Jana Sangh, proponent of Integral Humanism -> (II)
Matching: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText: Which of the following statement is correct about Charu Majumdar?

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Assumed both statements were correct.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies that both statements contain factual errors.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Charu Majumdar was an active member of the Communist Party of India and participated in the historic Tebhaga Movement in Bengal in 1946. Later, he broke away from the CPI(M) to lead the armed Naxalbari peasant revolt in 1967 and founded the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) in 1969.
Hence, option (B) is correct.

questionText: What does not relate to the effects of globalization on the world?

options.text:
Greater trade among countries allows each economy to do what it does
best.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text:
Developed countries have carefully guarded their borders with visa
policies.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Globalization has led to the shrinking of our choices to a large extent
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Syllabus Core.

options.text:
The restrictions on movement of capital across countries have been
reduced
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Syllabus Core (Crises of the Constitutional Order):
Evaluation of statements:
- (A) Globalization expands and broadens choices (commodities, food, culture, communication) rather than shrinking them. Hence, statement A does NOT represent the effect of globalization.
- (B) Greater trade promotes economic comparative advantage, allowing economies to focus on what they do best.
- (C) Developed countries strictly regulate immigration using visa regimes while demanding free flow of goods and capital.
- (D) Capital mobility has been extensively deregulated and liberalized worldwide.
Therefore, option A is the statement that does not relate correctly to the effects of globalization.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
